title: Double knit mittens
subtitle: Reversible mittens in two colours worked using the double knitting technique.
excerpt: Full mittens in two-colour double knitting, producing a reversible fabric with one colour on each side. DK weight, worked in the round. The double knitting technique creates a thick, draught-proof fabric without separate layers. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Double knitting is documented in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), Alasdair Post-Quinn, Extreme Double Knitting (2011), and in multiple traditional Nordic knitting publications. The technique is cross-referenced across 5 or more published sources.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts x 28 rounds for the combined double-knit fabric = 10 x 10 cm on 4 mm needles. Each side has 11 sts per 10 cm of visible fabric.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A technique where two layers of knitting are worked simultaneously on one set of needles. Each stitch pair consists of one stitch for the front layer (knitted) and one for the back layer (purled). The front yarn and back yarn swap between each pair, creating a reversible two-colour fabric with one colour on each side.

A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches on both layers which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

In double knitting, every visible stitch on the needle is actually a pair: one stitch for the outer fabric and one for the inner. The yarn is swapped between each pair so that MC knits the outer stitches (kept in front) and CC knits the inner stitches (sent to the back). The result is a tube of double-layered fabric: warm and draught-proof. The construction uses
on a long circular. Budget about 90 g of each colour (200 m / 220 yards each), both DK. Double knitting is slow; allow about twice the time of a single-layer mitten.

content.text: 22 combined stitches (11 per layer) and 28 rounds to 10 cm on 4 mm needles. Swatch in double knitting specifically. The needles are one size larger than standard DK because the double fabric is denser.

attrs.heading: Every stitch is a pair: (MC knit, CC purl). All rounds RS.

items.name: Setup
items.qty: Cast on with both colours alternating: *1 MC stitch, 1 CC stitch*, repeat. Use a two-colour cast-on or cast on all MC then work the CC stitches in on the first round.

items.name: Every round
items.qty: *Bring both yarns to back, k1 MC; bring both yarns to front, p1 CC*; repeat to end.

items.name: Yarn management
items.qty: Keep MC always above CC when both are at front. Drop the non-working yarn to the opposite position before each stitch.

content.text: Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm. Note: all counts below are total stitches on the needle (both layers combined).
Cast on 80 (88, 96) total stitches in alternating MC and CC pairs. Join to work in the round. Work double knitting for 28 (30, 32) rounds. The cuff measures about 10 (11, 11) cm.

Continue double knitting for 12 (14, 14) rounds. Place the thumb: work the first 20 (22, 24) paired stitches with waste yarn, slip back, and work in double knitting to end. Continue for 24 (26, 28) more rounds.

Work the top decreases by treating each pair as one stitch for the decrease, then recreating the pair. A double-knit k2tog: k2tog in MC, p2tog in CC across the adjacent pairs. Place a midpoint marker and work 4 decreases per decrease round (one pair at each edge, front and back). Repeat until 8 total stitches remain. Join the two layers by knitting each MC stitch together with its adjacent CC stitch. Draw yarn through.
Remove waste yarn and pick up paired stitches from the thumb gap: 20 (22, 24) pairs above and 20 (22, 24) below. Work 16 (18, 18) rounds of double knitting. Join the layers and close as for the top.

Layers join at the sides: both yarns were in the same position (both front or both back) when moving between pairs. The MC knit stitch must have both yarns at back; the CC purl stitch must have both yarns at front. The swap must happen between every single stitch.

Colours bleed through to the wrong side: the MC stitch was worked with CC or vice versa. Keep the yarn colours in strict alternation: the stitch on the needle always matches the yarn about to knit it.
Weave each colour tail into the matching layer on the wrong side.
Hand wash in cool water with wool-safe detergent. The double-layer fabric takes longer to dry than single-layer mittens. Lay flat and turn inside out halfway through drying.
Once the basic double-knit structure is secure, colour motifs can be worked by swapping which yarn knits the outer stitch at specific positions. This is the foundation of double-knit Fair Isle.
